  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   --job-name=br5_FPointNet
#   --partition=gpu
#   --mem=16G
#   --ntasks-per-node=32
#   --time=0-72:00:00
#   --output=/home/jbandl2s/train.%j.out
#   --error=/home/jbandl2s/train.%j.err
#   --gres=gpu:0

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 32 \
  --time=72h \
  --queue=gpu \
  bash -lc '

# NOTE: Slurm --mem=16G has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: Slurm --job-name=br5_FPointNet is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

# NOTE: Slurm output/error used %j substitution; we approximate with ${FLUX_JOB_ID}.
exec >"/home/jbandl2s/train.${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>"/home/jbandl2s/train.${FLUX_JOB_ID}.err"

# NOTE: Slurm --gres=gpu:0 explicitly requests no GPUs.
# This is preserved by not requesting GPUs in Flux. On a GPU partition this may still land on GPU-capable nodes.
# Performance implication: if the application actually uses GPUs, it will not have an allocated GPU resource.

module load cuda

source ~/anaconda3/bin/activate ~/anaconda3/envs/3DOD_Env

cd /home/jbandl2s/sub_ensembles/models

DATA_FILE="/scratch/jbandl2s/Lyft_dataset/artifacts/frustums_train"
MODEL_LOG_DIR="./log_v1_test/"
RESTORE_MODEL_PATH="./log_v1_test/model.ckpt"

python train_branch_15.py
'
"
}
